primary_secondary.note: Both: DORA research team presents its own model, built from 78 interviews and the annual DORA survey (~5,000 respondents).

dora_applied.claude: Yes (empirical) (DORA AI Capabilities Model proposed and evaluated with the DORA survey)
dora_applied.nlm: unclear (model 'discussed and introduced'; notes traditional DORA delivery metrics are not named)
dora_applied.note: Post introduces DORA's own AI Capabilities Model with survey-based results, but the four DORA delivery metrics are not used; neither extractor settles the level.

ai_discussed.note: Capabilities that amplify the benefits of AI-assisted software development.

remote_covid.note: Neither mentions remote work or COVID-19.

data_window.note: Not stated by either; only the 'annual survey' (~5,000 respondents) without a collection period.

cat_productivity.claude: No (outcomes such as individual effectiveness and team/organizational performance are survey-measured, i.e. perceptual)
cat_productivity.nlm: Yes (individual effectiveness, team, organizational and product performance as performance outcomes)
cat_productivity.note: Same outcomes listed by both; Claude marks them as measured via survey (perceived), NotebookLM presents them as performance dimensions.

cat_quality.note: Code quality as an outcome amplified by AI-accessible internal data; rollback/revert as safety net.

cat_satisfaction.note: 'Friction' for employees/teams is an outcome, but neither frames it as satisfaction/well-being.

cat_activity.note: Thin basis: frequent commits (and rollback use) as version-control capability indicators.

cat_delivery.note: NotebookLM explicitly notes DORA delivery metrics are not named.

cat_agile.note: Working in small batches is one of the seven capabilities, not treated as a process metric by either.

cat_survey.note: Validated survey questions; annual DORA survey with almost 5,000 respondents; 78 interviews.

evidence.quote: Title: Introducing DORA’s inaugural AI Capabilities Model | Google Cloud Blog
The DORA research team has developed the inaugural DORA AI Capabilities Model to provide data-backed guidance for organizations grappling with these questions.

Second, we developed and validated survey questions to ensure they were clear, reliable, and measured each capability accurately. Lastly, we evaluated the impact of a subset of these candidates using the rigorous methodology of designing and analyzing our annual survey—which reached almost 5,000 respondents.
evidence.loc: text source (The DORA AI Capabilities Model: 7 levers of success)

evidence.quote: Connecting AI tools to internal data sources boosts their impact on individual effectiveness and code quality.
Specifically, frequent commits amplify AI's positive influence on individual effectiveness, while the frequent use of rollback features boosts the performance of AI-assisted teams.
